reply.text:
Let me check what your long runs actually look like first. Nothing is logged for your runs, program or goals yet, so I'm going on general coaching here.

Legs fading in the last mile usually comes down to three things: starting the long run too fast, building distance too quickly, or not having enough leg strength and weekly volume behind the long run. The fixes are mostly boring:

1. Run the first half of the long run truly easy, slow enough that you could hold a conversation. If you finish the last mile feeling strong, you can push it next time.
2. Add distance gradually. A long run that grows a little each week, with an easier week every third or fourth, lets the legs adapt.
3. Add a second, shorter easy run during the week so the long run isn't most of your mileage.
4. Lift legs once or twice a week. Squats, lunges, step-ups, and calf work make the late miles easier.
5. Fuel and drink on runs past about an hour, since running low on fuel feels exactly like heavy legs.

If you tell me how many days you run, your longest run, and whether you have a race in mind, I can build you a plan around it.
